metadata.title: QQC-001: NanoDrop Nucleic Acid Quantification - Thermo Fisher NanoDrop One
metadata.purpose: Pedestal measurement for DNA/RNA concentration and A260/A280 / A260/A230 purity ratios
metadata.scope: Training/library SOP draft. Confirm against the current instrument manual, kit insert, SDS, and local lab policy before bench use.
beforeYouBegin: Use the same solution as the blank that best matches the sample matrix, such as elution buffer or nuclease-free water.
Mix samples well and briefly spin down. Avoid bubbles, particulates, and sample droplets on tube caps.
Clean pedestal before blanking and between samples. Residue causes carryover and abnormal ratios.
Use NanoDrop as a purity screen. UV absorbance cannot distinguish target nucleic acid from free nucleotides, phenol, RNA/DNA mixture, or other absorbers.

materials.name: Sample buffer for blanking
materials.specification: Use the same solution as the blank that best matches the sample matrix, such as elution buffer or nuclease-free water

materials.name: Qubit assay
materials.specification: Optional orthogonal concentration confirmation; more target-specific for low-concentration samples or library prep

steps.action: Open the appropriate nucleic acid application on the NanoDrop One instrument.
Clean upper and lower pedestals with nuclease-free water and lint-free wipe, then dry fully.
Load blank solution onto the lower pedestal using the instrument-recommended volume.
Lower the arm and perform blank measurement.
Wipe both pedestals clean and dry.
Mix sample gently. Load sample onto the pedestal without introducing bubbles.

parameters.rawText: Common quick QC method requiring 1-2 uL sample and reporting concentration plus purity ratios.

steps.action: Lower the arm and measure sample.
Review concentration, A260/A280, A260/A230, and absorbance spectrum shape.

acceptanceCriteria.description: DNA A260/A280 is often near 1.8; RNA is often near 2.0. Interpret with extraction chemistry and sample type.
DNA A260/A280 is often near 1.8; RNA is often near 2.0. Interpret with extraction chemistry and sample type.
Low A260/A230 suggests salts, phenol, guanidinium, carbohydrates, ethanol, or other contaminants.
Abnormal spectra, high blank, or inconsistent replicates require cleaning, reblanking, dilution, or orthogonal measurement.

steps.expectedResult: Concentration, purity ratios, and absorbance spectrum shape are reviewed.

steps.action: Wipe pedestals between samples and repeat measurement for technical replicate if accuracy is important.

repeat.notes: Repeat measurement for technical replicate if accuracy is important; the source gives no fixed replicate count.

steps.action: Export or record sample ID, application type, concentration, purity ratios, and any alert flags.
For low-concentration samples or library prep, confirm with Qubit because it is more target-specific.

controls.name: Matched blank
controls.description: Use the same solution as the blank that best matches the sample matrix, such as elution buffer or nuclease-free water.

controls.name: Technical replicate
controls.description: Wipe pedestals between samples and repeat measurement for technical replicate if accuracy is important.

expectedOutputs: Absorbance spectrum shape, alert flags, and completed measurement record.

troubleshooting.cause: Contaminants or mixed nucleic acid absorbing at 260 nm.
troubleshooting.solution: Use Qubit-specific assay and inspect A230/A280/spectrum.

troubleshooting.cause: Dirty pedestal, bubbles, evaporation, poor mixing.

troubleshooting.solution: Repeat cleanup or precipitation; dry sample appropriately.
Use matched blank and clean instrument.

safety: Wear lab coat, gloves, and eye protection. Treat nucleic acids, cells, dyes, chips, ScreenTape, cuvettes, and biological cultures according to local EHS and biosafety rules.
Avoid contaminating shared instruments. Wipe pedestals, cuvette holders, fluorometer tube chambers, and work surfaces according to instrument-compatible cleaning guidance.
Use nuclease-free consumables for RNA/DNA QC. Use RNase-free handling for RNA integrity checks.
Do not overinterpret a single number. Pair concentration with purity ratios, fluorometric specificity, integrity metrics, and sample context.
Record sample ID, dilution, blank/buffer, instrument ID, assay kit/lot, measurement mode, replicate values, calculated concentration, and pass/fail notes.
